harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a systemd-managed, sandboxed background worker named inventory-worker on node1, confirmed it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory and gains no new privileges, then completed the mandatory single-node restart-evidence protocol showing boot identity change and full service/data recovery.
actions_performed: Created dedicated system user inventory-worker with home /var/lib/inventory (no login shell)
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh, a POSIX loop that writes state.json/worker.log into /var/lib/inventory every 5s

Installed /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=yes, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, PrivateTmp/PrivateDevices, empty CapabilityBoundingSet/AmbientCapabilities, RestrictNamespaces/SUIDSGID/Realtime, LockPersonality, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, UMask=0027
Enabled and started the service; verified active/running and enabled for boot
Verified confinement via nsenter into the unit's mount namespace: write to /etc fails with Read-only file system while write to /var/lib/inventory succeeds
Verified NoNewPrivs=1 and CapBnd=0 in /proc/<pid>/status, and ran systemd-analyze security (overall exposure 3.6 OK)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/data baseline
Issued `systemctl reboot` via backgrounded nohup so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again and confirmed boot_id changed
Post-restart: confirmed service auto-started (active/enabled), worker resumed writing new ticks to state.json/worker.log, and sandbox restrictions (read-only /etc, NoNewPrivs=1) still held

evidence.requirement: Managed service named inventory-worker running as a long-running background worker
evidence.summary: systemctl status/is-active/is-enabled show inventory-worker.service active and enabled, PID present, state.json/worker.log being written continuously
nsenter into the running unit's mount namespace shows write to /etc fails (Read-only file system) while write to /var/lib/inventory succeeds, proving ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths confinement

/proc/<pid>/status shows NoNewPrivs=1 and CapBnd=0000000000000000 (empty capability bounding set), and systemd-analyze security confirms NoNewPrivileges=, CapabilityBoundingSet= and AmbientCapabilities= are all satisfied
Captured boot_id 31b01b46-... plus active/enabled service state and current state.json/worker.log data before reboot
systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded nohup; command returned reboot-issued pid before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves actual restart (node1)
evidence.summary: Connection timed out while node was rebooting, then exec succeeded again with boot_id c220ee7e-... (changed from baseline 31b01b46-...) and uptime 0 min

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required service, data, and sandbox constraints (node1)
evidence.summary: After restart, inventory-worker.service is active/enabled, worker.log/state.json show fresh ticks resuming from tick=1, and nsenter/proc checks confirm /etc is still read-only and NoNewPrivs=1 persisted

attempts.summary: Deployed a systemd-managed, sandboxed background worker named inventory-worker on node1, confirmed it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory and gains no new privileges, then completed the mandatory single-node restart-evidence protocol showing boot identity change and full service/data recovery.
